name: お寺カフェ (Otera Cafe)
cuisine: Cafe / shojin okayu (Buddhist rice porridge) / wagashi
gf_detail: Shojin cuisine often inherently avoids gluten-containing ingredients, but the use of soy sauce (contains wheat) and fu (wheat gluten) is unclear. No stated gluten-free accommodation. Celiacs should always inquire before visiting (026-234-0001). NOT confirmed celiac-safe.

name: マルベリーデリカテッセンアンドカフェ (Mulberry Delicatessen and Cafe)
gf_detail: No gluten-free labeling found on the menu or website. Bread and quiche are central offerings, and pasta is a regular feature — wheat is pervasive. Some deli sides (e.g., ratatouille, vegetable escabeche) may be naturally wheat-free, but cross-contamination risk in a busy deli kitchen is unassessed and no dedicated GF protocols are mentioned. name: おやき屋 (Oyaki-ya)
gf_detail: Oyaki are wrapped in a wheat-flour dough — not gluten-free.

name: 山の間 (Yamanoma Brewery & Craft Beer Pub)
gf_detail: A brewpub — the craft beer itself contains gluten. Some kitchen dishes may be gluten-free; ask which are wheat/soy-free.

name: 野菜カフェ ヒューマンズ (Yasai Café Humans)
gf_detail: A vegetable-forward vegetarian/vegan café; GF is plausible for many dishes but unconfirmed — ask which are wheat/soy-free.

name: いろは堂 MIDORI長野店 (Irohado)
gf_detail: A Togakushi oyaki maker that is noted to offer a gluten-free option alongside its wheat-dough oyaki — confirm which items are the GF version.

name: 小川の庄 おやき村 MIDORI長野店 (Ogawa-no-shō Oyaki-mura)
gf_detail: Oyaki wrapped in wheat-flour dough — not gluten-free.

name: カフェ・モンマルトル (Café Montmartre)
gf_detail: Curry with all-you-can-eat naan — naan is wheat; rice + some curries may be GF. Ask about wheat in the roux.

name: インド料理 サンディア (Sandia)
gf_detail: Indian — rice, dal and many curries are naturally GF, but naan is wheat and some sauces use flour/dairy. Ask for rice + GF curries.
